summary: This work demonstrates that polaron formation due to qubit-environment entanglement limits dissipative reset fidelity in transmon qubits, and shows this can be overcome by time-dependent control of the system-environment coupling. Optimized smooth switching protocols achieve excited-state populations of $10^{-6}$ in 10 ns at zero temperature, with achievable protocols reaching $10^{-6.5}$.
motivation: Dissipative reset is crucial for superconducting qubits, but non-Markovian effects limit speed and fidelity; understanding and controlling system-environment entanglement beyond the Born-Markov approximation offers a path to faster, higher-fidelity reset.
method: The authors use exact tensor-network TEMPO simulations and the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) applied to the polaron ansatz for the spin-boson model with Ohmic spectral density ($\alpha = 0.03$, $\omega_q/2\pi = 5$ GHz, $\omega_c = \omega_q$) to study time-dependent coupling protocols $u(t)$. Optimal decoupling functions are found via linear-quadratic regulator control theory.
result: Linear switching reduces residual population by two orders of magnitude; smoother protocols with exponent $\lambda = 2$ achieve $P_+ \approx 10^{-6.5}$ at zero temperature in $\sim 10$ ns, compared to $P_+ \sim 10^{-3}$ over hundreds of nanoseconds in current experiments, limited ultimately by thermal population $\sim 10^{-5}$ at 20 mK.
